structure: Independent people sampled from a trivariate Gaussian distribution with the exact population means and covariance implied by the records. Gaussian shape is a modeling assumption; all three requested population functionals are identified without it.

parameter_provenance.basis: Population means in X, Y, Z order.
Population individual variances in X, Y, Z order.
A supplies marginal XY; B supplies marginal XZ and YZ.
Covariances equal correlations because all three population variances are one.
Population OLS residuals are X-0.6Z and Y-0.6Z. Each residual variance is 1-0.6^2; their covariance is 0.5-0.6*0.6.
Chosen joint shape; the supplied moments do not determine a distribution.

requested_estimands.name: partial_xy_given_z
requested_estimands.basis: Pearson correlation of separate population OLS residuals after intercept and measured-Z adjustment: (0.5-0.6*0.6)/sqrt((1-0.6^2)*(1-0.6^2)) = 0.14/0.64.

requested_estimands.name: slope_x_on_z
requested_estimands.basis: The population OLS slope with an intercept is Cov(X,Z)/Var(Z) = 0.6/1 using B and C.

limitations: Gaussian shape, tails, and higher-order dependence are assumed, not identified by the records.
Population moments are exact constraints on the generating distribution; realized sample moments and fitted estimates fluctuate naturally and are not forced to equal them.
The adjusted estimand is a linear-residual Pearson correlation, not a causal effect or a generally specified conditional correlation.
These artificial records provide no biomedical validation.
checks_actually_performed: Analytically checked positive definiteness: the covariance matrix has leading principal minors 1, 0.75, and 0.39.
Algebraically checked residual variances of 0.64, residual covariance of 0.14, and residual correlation of 0.21875.
Inspected the source for seeded independent sampling, unique integer identifiers, requested column order, and absence of sample-moment forcing.
No code execution or finite-sample empirical checks were performed.
